compute.reported_as: The length of the SSE runs generating these results were adapted to achieve a statistical error less than 3 x 10^-8 in the energy (rounded to one digit in the table). [...] The results for L <= 30 represent averages over simulations at beta/L = 32 and 64. [...] The calculations reported here were mostly limited to beta/L <= 64 and system sizes L <= 96, with some limited test results generated also at beta/L = 128 for L = 80, 88, and 96. [...] As an example of the computational effort involved to generate the data presented here, in the case of the L = 96 system at inverse temperature beta = 64L, one full SSE updating sweep with measurements of observables required about 10 s using Intel Xeon Gold 6000-series CPUs. Approximately 1.5 x 10^8 such steps were performed, for a total of about 4 x 10^5 hours of CPU core time, distributed over a large number of CPU cores. In the case of L = 8 at beta = 32L, an updating sweep takes about 1e-3 s and about 2 x 10^11 steps were carried out for a total of about 5 x 10^4 core hours (and this accounted for about half of the statistics for this system size, the remainder coming from beta = 64L runs). [...] The numerical calculations were carried out on the Shared Computing Cluster managed by Boston University's Research Computing Services.
compute.source: Sec. II.3 'Tabulated numerical data' (Table 1 note); Sec. II.2 (beta/L limits); Sec. V (computational-effort paragraph before Acknowledgements); Acknowledgements, arXiv:2601.20189 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: No per-size cost is stated for this row; the paper gives worked examples only for L = 96 (periodic, beta = 64L: ~4e5 CPU core hours, ~1.5e8 sweeps of ~10 s each on Intel Xeon Gold 6000-series CPUs) and L = 8 (periodic, beta = 32L: ~5e4 core hours for about half the statistics), and states that run lengths were adapted to reach an energy error below 3e-8 (periodic Table 1). All calculations ran on Boston University's Shared Computing Cluster (CPU); core counts and wall-clock are not stated ('distributed over a large number of CPU cores').
